Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Game Overview 1.1 Turn Order 1.2 Coaches 1.3 Game End 2 Sports Overview 2.1 Sport Climbing 2.2 Golf 2.3 Rowing 2.4 Hurdles 2.5 Skateboarding 2.6 Triple Jump 3 Solo Variant 3.1 Sport Climbing 3.2 Golf 3.3 Rowing 3.4 Hurdles 3.5 Skateboarding 3.6 Triple Jump Game Overview Turn Order The First Player rolls the dice. They choose and remove one die and write the number into one of the valid boxes for any sport. The player on their right chooses a die from the remaining dice and writes the number into one of the valid boxes for any sport. This is repeated until the first player chooses a second die. The player on the right of the first player becomes the first player for the next round. If a player cannot write a number on their game sheet, they must pass and the game is now over for them. Coaches Each player has 3 coaches which they can use before they choose a die. Re-Roll - This re-rolls all the dice that are left in the dice pool. Flip a Die - This changes the selected die to the number on the opposite side (eg from a 6 to 1). Add 1 to a Die - This increases the selected die's value by 1. You may not increase a 6 to a 7. Game End Once all players have passed the game is over and medals are then awarded for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place in each sport. Each medal is worth Victory Points (gold is 5 points, silver is 3 points and bronze is 1 point). The player with the most points at the end of the game wins. (Quick Mode Option) If Quick Mode is activated when the table is created, the turn order is handled differently. Quick Mode means that every player rolls 6 dice and chooses one from these dice. They then pass the remaining dice to next player. This will be repeated to the end of available dice, then every player rolls again. This will be repeated 7 times, then the game is over. Sports Overview Sport Climbing Sport Climbing is a race to the top. On their turn players may cross off the lowest number on the climbing wall. The first player to cross off the 6 is the winner. If the game ends with nobody reaching the top, whoever made it the furthest wins. Golf In Golf players must complete the course using the fewest dice. To complete a hole the sum of the dice used must add up to greater than or equal to the number in the flag. Holes must be completed in order. The winner is whoever finished the course with the least amount of dice used. In case of a tie, lowest sum of dice wins. In the case no player finished the course, the player with more holes completed is considered the winner. Rowing In rowing, each rowboat must have a matching pair (top and bottom). Players must also complete the first boat before filling in the next boat. At the end of the game the highest total from completed boats wins. In case of a tie, the least boats used wins. Hurdles In Hurdles the sheet must be filled from left to right. Any dice over hurdles must be greater than 3. The course must be filled to score. Lowest total sum wins. Skateboarding Skateboarding is made up of 3 different tricks. You may begin filling in any trick you wish and they don't need to be completely filled to score. Highest total wins. Kickflip - Muiltply both numbers. Frontside 5-0 Grind - Numbers must be in consecutive descending order (e.g. 5 - 4 - 3) Starting from the left. Handplant - All numbers must be equal. Triple Jump In the Triple Jump, players start by filling in the first 3 numbers. These must be in consecutive ascending order (e.g. 4 - 5 - 6). The following numbers must be equal. community_text:
[Rating: 2/10] Roll and write game where you try to score based on different events or scoring rules. Quite boring and artwork is meh too.

[Rating: 2.6/10] roll and write game draft a dice and write on the papers simply too random and not much action choice available  little game variation

[Rating: 3/10] Less interesting than average roll and write. I feel like there aren't really decisions here as much as you just kinda play the dice you can. The way many of the sports are set up mean that you are regularly going after the same die values. You have three modifiers to use for the whole game, which, again, means that you regularly just place the die you can and hope it works out better next time.

[Rating: 4/10] There's 100 other games that are like this but better. It's also particularly poorly designed for 2p - there are 6 courses, so a pretty common scenario is that each player will win 3 of them and then you have a tie in a large fraction of games.

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Meh, it is fine for a roll and write I suppose but it did nothing new or exciting that would pull me in for another play. Feel like there are a couple other games that do this better.

[Rating: 4/10] I don't think I'd want to play this opposed, though the Me-you-me dice selection may make it interesting.  It's on BGA and I played two games. It's pleasant to pass the time for a solo experience.

[Rating: 4/10] Another push your luck game on BGA. It's alright, but the scoring and everything is a bit cumbersome.
